candidates.changed_node: the range lookback window: all three literals 21 -> 63 in TS_MIN($low, 21), TS_MAX($high, 21), TS_MIN($low, 21)
candidates.rationale: Weakness is a monotone fade, not turnover or noise: IC runs +0.025/+0.016/+0.028 in 2000-2002 and collapses to +0.0027/+0.0010 in 2012-2013, with turnover 0.099 and half-life 19.3 days both healthy. The component responsible is the 21-day range window, which makes this a short-horizon reversal proxy, and that premium faded in large caps after 2009. Widening the range to 63 days moves it off the crowded 21-day cluster (memory 1) into the medium niche (memory 5) while staying well short of the 189-day archive high, preserving rho headroom against the 0.608 neighbour. Numerator anchor, denominator form and epsilon guard untouched.

This is a regime problem localized to one leg. The two negative years are 2003 (-0.0054) and 2013 (-0.0045), plus near-zero 2009 (+0.0047) and 2010 (+0.0016): those are exactly the risk-on recovery years. CS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 126)) is a defensive low-vol bet that earns in 2000-2002 and 2008 and gives it back whenever high-vol names lead, so it carries the cycle. Replacing that leg with a slow dollar-volume scaler keeps the multiplicative form (memory 2) and uses volume over a long window as a scaler rather than a same-day multiplier (memory 8), while dropping the vol-regime exposure. The position-under-189-day-high leg is left intact because that is the part memory 5 credits, and the 189-day warm-up is unchanged so coverage stays at 0.904.

candidates.changed_node: the $roa leaf: level -> TS_DELTA($roa, 252), year-over-year change
candidates.rationale: The weak component is the level form of the leaf, not the rank wrapper. As a static profitability level it sits at |rho| 0.723 against the archive quality composite CS_RANK($operating_margin * $asset_turnover) - CS_RANK($leverage), the tightest correlation of any parent here, and its two negative years (2003 -0.0045, 2006 -0.0026) are the junk-rally years when a quality level is on the wrong side. Wrapping the leaf in a 252-day delta converts level to four-quarter change: it stays a slow standalone fundamental as memory 3 requires, compares like quarters so report seasonality cancels, and a change series is largely orthogonal to the level-based archive member, which is what buys back the correlation headroom. Half-life should stay long and turnover near zero.

The diagnostics say this is an exposure rather than a signal: IC half-life never halves inside 63 days, three negative years (2003, 2005, 2007), ICIR 0.044, and |rho| 0.717 against plain $volume. All of that traces to the TS_MEAN aggregator, which returns a cross-sectional size/liquidity level that barely moves. Replacing it with a within-name time-series rank over the stock's own 252 days strips the static size level and leaves only the abnormal-activity part, which gives the signal actual time variation (a finite half-life) and breaks the near-duplicate with $volume. Volume is used over a long window as memory 8 prescribes, and turnover stays low since a 252-day rank moves slowly.

candidates.changed_node: the EMA lookback literal: EMA($close, 10) -> EMA($close, 42)
candidates.rationale: Two diagnostics point at the same node: this has the highest turnover in the population (0.292 one-way, 0.007 of fitness) and the shortest half-life (3.1 days), and it is negative in four of the last seven years (2007, 2010, 2011, 2012). The EMA(10) reference sets the horizon, and 10 days is faster than the edge survives, so the factor churns daily for an IC that is gone within three days. Slowing the reference to 42 days stretches the half-life toward the holding horizon and cuts the turnover charge, and it pushes the reversion window well away from the 21-day cluster flagged in memory 1. The TS_STD($close, 21) denominator is deliberately left alone: memory 4 records that short-horizon reversal only survived when divided by trailing realized volatility.

At t 0.16 and fitness 0.090 the dead component is the denominator. TS_SUM(ABS($return), 63) turns a 63-day signed return sum into a bounded path-efficiency ratio, which normalizes away the magnitude of the move and leaves a sign-only statistic whose IC half-life is 3.3 days despite the long window. Memory 6 says to stop re-deriving that ratio, and this slot is the one worth displacing. Swapping the denominator to TS_STD($return, 63) keeps the same 63-day numerator and turns it into risk-adjusted medium-horizon momentum, the one return form that has survived on this island (memory 4), with a scale that varies across names and regimes instead of collapsing to [-1, 1]. Nearest archive rho was only 0.313, so there is room.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.
